title: add change-point latency detector and automated cutover safety guard
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: We observed intermittent latency plateaus that are not captured by simple percentile thresholding; this PR introduces a statistical change-point detector tuned for low-volume but persistent shifts and an automated 'cutover safety guard' that can pause or reroute rollouts when a sustained change-point is detected. Design summary: (1) lightweight online change-point detector based on Bayesian Online Change Point Detection (BOCPD) with an optional PELT fallback for batched analysis; detector runs over request latency fingerprints (p50/p90/p99 + jitter) and uses a configurable persistence window before triggering a safety action. (2) Cutover safety guard: a controller that subscribes to canary evaluation streams and enforces transient hold/rollback/circuit-routing policies; integrates with the existing canary-controller and rollout API so that interruptions are audited and reversible. (3) Telemetry and observability: new metrics for cp_detection_score, cp_persistence_secs, safety_guard_action and a compact alert set mapped to on-call rotation. Backwards compatibility: the detector is opt-in per-canary via a feature flag and default configuration is conservative (high precision, lower sensitivity). Rollout plan: staged roll-out to internal perf canaries for 48 hours, then opt-in for customer canaries behind a feature flag; signal collection and thresholds will be tuned in a 2-week validation period. Testing: unit tests for detector edge cases, simulated traces harness that injects change events and SLO regressions, end-to-end integration with canary controller in perf lab. Performance: the online detector is implemented to operate in O(1) amortized per-sample and adds <0.2% CPU at 99th percentile on our canary-controller instances in lab. TODOs and follow-ups: add auto-tuning for persistence window, surface per-model profiles in Optimize recommendations, and add a lightweight JS/TS client for SDKs. Related: addresses ENG-4829 and supports SUP-2101 incident mitigation.

review_comments: Marco Diaz: Please explain false positive rate characteristics and how operator noise (rolling restarts) affects CP signals. Author reply: Added a dedicated section in the runbook and included a persistence window default of 300s to dampen restart noise; unit tests include simulated restarts.

Priya Shah: Can we avoid Python CPU hotspots when detector is used at high QPS? Suggest migrating heavy math to C/Go or Numpy vectorization. Author reply: Detector is O(1) per-sample; heavy math is limited to occasional batch fallback (PELT) that runs in background. We agreed to monitor CPU in perf lab and consider a Go rewrite if usage grows.

Liam O'Connor: What happens to metrics continuity when guard holds a rollout? Author reply: The controller emits safety_guard_action with reason labels and creates a synthetic annotation event in the existing canary timeline so downstream dashboards show the hold and why.

QA (automated): Found flaky test test_change_detector_noise_handling - initial failure on CI run 1, rerun passed after increasing fixture timeout. Author reply: test timeout increased and fixture stabilization added.
Marco Diaz: approved after addressing noise tests and adding runbook entry.
Priya Shah: approved (code review + perf numbers checked).
release_notes: Add an opt-in online change-point latency detector and a safety guard controller that can pause or reroute rollouts when persistent latency shifts are detected. Controlled rollout behind feature flag, with runbook and dashboards. Impact: improves detection of persistent regressions that percentile-based detectors miss.
notes: Merged after 2 approvals and CI green. Feature behind 'perf.canary.change_point_detector' flag by default off for customer canaries.
Perf bench shows <0.2% CPU overhead at tested load; PELT fallback runs asynchronously to avoid p99 spikes.
Follow-ups: auto-tune persistence window, Go port for high-QPS path, SDK example in TS
